correctness.rationale: Reconstructed H_N=⊕_{k=0}^N D_k, dim=(N+1)(N+2)/2. P_N M_{az+bw} maps D_k to D_{k+1} for k<N and kills D_N; the (k+2)x(k+1) full-column-rank bidiagonal block has Gram diagonal A²+B² and off-diagonal a* conjugate(b), unitarily gauged to AB. The sine eigenvectors yield s_{j,r}²=A²+B²+2AB cos(pi r/j), 2<=j<=N+1, 1<=r<j, strictly positive even if A=0 or B=0. Therefore N(N+1)/2 positive singulars and N+1 zero ones, with exact extreme values. For A!=B the bounded Riemann sum gives Q/N²->(1/(2pi)) integral_0^pi f(theta)^(-p/2)dtheta for all p>0 including a zero coefficient. When A=B=c>0, t=j-r yields 2c sin(pi t/(2j)); endpoint integrability for p<1, harmonic sums for p=1, t^-p dominated convergence for p>1 give each stated constant. Summing cosecant² gives exact Q_N,2=N(N+1)(2N+7)/(36c²). In the near-balance a_N=c+tau/(2N), b_N=c-tau/(2N), fixed p>1, s²=(tau/N)²+4A_NB_N sin²(pi t/(2j)); after multiplying by N² the pointwise limit is tau²+(pi ct/u)² at j/N->u. Uniform t^-p(j/N)^p majorant validates both limit exchanges including u=0; the coth summation for p=2 is correct. Independently built full compressed matrices and checked 40 complex-parameter/N cases; the maximum singular-value discrepancy was 8.9e-16. Symbolic exact p=2 finite trace identity verified; direct balanced ratios and p=2 critical-window ratios converge numerically. These tests corroborate but are not proofs of asymptotics.
residual_risks: The infinite estimates rely on analytic dominated-convergence and endpoint-sum arguments; no machine-checked formal proof is claimed.
Numerical p<1 ratios at N<=1400 are still 0.95 due slow endpoint convergence, consistent with the analytic limit and not proof from extrapolation.
Fixed p and tau are required in the window; no uniformity over p or N-dependent tau was established.

value.rationale: The total-degree finite section of a bidisk Hardy linear multiplier is a natural graded Toeplitz compression with a rank-deficient Moore-Penrose inverse. Its conditioning changes sharply at equal coefficient moduli. Determining the full spectral multiset, exact inverse-square finite trace, three distinct inverse-moment growth laws, and a nontrivial mass-dependent critical-window function quantifies a mathematically motivated transition at natural scale N^-1; this is useful for benchmark inverse regularization of graded multivariable shifts. The crossover is not a gratuitous finite numeric statistic or merely a renamed tridiagonal eigenvalue identity. Value remains narrow: only linear symbols and this cutoff, no general polygon or higher-dimensional theorem asserted.
residual_risks: Significance is specific to the unweighted total-degree Hardy bidisk model; no broader Toeplitz theorem or computational regularization algorithm is established.
Some component methods (sine diagonalization, harmonic/coth summation) are elementary; value rests on the naturally motivated complete inverse-moment classification including the N^-1 crossover.
